kicker: Restaurants, bars, cafés and multi-unit groups
lede: Thirty-two small agents that check a restaurant's back office from the files it already exports, food cost, labor, tips, cash, delivery apps, fees, tax and compliance, and wait for a named person before anything is paid, sent or changed.
packages: Actual against theoretical food cost, recipe costs, vendor price creep, deliveries and credits, counts, waste and 86s (7 agents)
Pour cost and liquor variance, menu engineering, discounts and promotions (3 agents)
Front of house and cash pack
Voids and comps, discounts, cash drawers, gift cards, no-shows, catering deposits (6 agents)
Tip pool and tip credit, overtime and split shifts, schedule against actual, labor by daypart, breaks and minors, set to your state (5 agents)
DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub payouts against orders, marketing fees, card processing fees (3 agents)
Sales tax by jurisdiction, duplicate invoices and GL coding, utility bills, weekly prime cost (4 agents)
Equipment maintenance, health inspections and permits, food handler cards, allergen matrix (4 agents)
All 31 single-location agents, mapped to your exports and set to your rules, one training session
Everything in Whole restaurant for each location, plus the location comparison against the group
For multi-unit groups, franchise operators and accounting firms serving many restaurants: all 32 agents, one shared setup, every location mapped
support: Support after setup: $150 a month for one pack, $300 a month for the whole restaurant, $200 a month per location for groups. Includes export changes, rule and rate updates, and a monthly check-in.
notes: Reads the files you export; it does not log in to your POS, scheduling, payroll, delivery-app, reservation, distributor or bank account.
Wage, tip, overtime, break, tax, inspection and allergen rules are settings you confirm with your accountant, payroll provider or health department; the defaults are examples.
Column layouts for Toast, Square, 7shifts, Sysco, DoorDash and the other named exports were written from knowledge of those systems; the first setup confirms them on your files.
Lost-sales and premium figures are estimates from your own numbers, not forecasts.
Not legal, tax, payroll, health-code or food-safety advice.
Report pages come in nine languages, translated by Claude and not yet reviewed by native speakers.
warn: Your files and reports stay on your computer. Staff and guest names are masked in anything sent to the AI model. No agent pays, refunds, charges a card, changes the POS, publishes a schedule, runs payroll, files taxes or messages anyone: drafts wait for one named person.
groups: Food, purchasing and the bar
Actual against theoretical food cost
What the recipes and sales say you used against what the counts and invoices say you did, per ingredient.
Recipe costs at latest invoice prices
Every plate costed at today's prices, with the menu price that would meet your target.
Vendor price creep
Price per pound or each across invoices, prices over your bid, packs that quietly got smaller.
Invoices against deliveries and credit memos
Shorts and cases refused at the door that were never credited.
Inventory count variance
Counts against expected, priced, and counts that look like the wrong unit.
Waste log
What was thrown out and why, and the days nobody logged anything.
Bar pour cost and liquor variance
Bottles used against drinks sold, per spirit, and pour cost against target.
Menu engineering
Stars, plowhorses, puzzles and dogs from your sales and plate costs.
Items 86ed and stockouts
Items that keep running out, for how long, and what that likely cost.
Front of house and cash
Voids and comps by employee
Self-approved voids, voids after payment, missing reasons, rates against sales.
Discounts and promotions
Promos used after they ended, outside their hours, over their cap, or not on your list.
Cash over and short by drawer
Expected cash against the count and the deposit, and shorts that repeat.
Gift card liability
What you still owe on cards, by location, and cards whose numbers do not add up.
Reservation no-shows
No-show rate, repeat no-shows, large parties with no deposit, fees your policy sets.
Catering deposits and balances
Deposits missing before the event, balances overdue after it, refunds owed.
Labor
Tip pool and tip credit
Pool shares by hours and role, and cash wage plus tips against the minimum for your state.
Overtime and split shifts
Weekly and daily overtime, double time, split shifts, spread of hours and clopens, priced.
Scheduled against actual labor
Early clock-ins, late clock-outs, no-shows and shifts nobody scheduled.
Labor percentage by daypart
Labor against sales for breakfast, lunch, dinner and late night.
Meal and rest breaks
Missed, short and late meals, and minors working too long or too late.
Delivery apps, fees, tax and bills
Delivery app payouts against orders
Commissions over your rate, short payouts, error charges and orders never paid.
Delivery app marketing fees
Ad and promo charges outside the campaigns you opted into, and what each campaign returned.
Card processing fees
Effective rate, markup over your agreement, and fees you never agreed to.
Sales tax by jurisdiction
Tax collected against your rates per location and category, marketplace orders kept apart.
Duplicate invoices and GL coding
Invoices entered twice, line math, and liquor or paper goods coded to food.
Utility bills
Usage spikes, rate jumps, estimated reads, duplicate bills and late fees.
Compliance and multi-unit
Equipment maintenance schedule
Hoods, grease traps, fire suppression and refrigeration overdue or coming up.
Health inspection calendar
Re-inspections due, critical violations not followed up, permits about to expire.
Food handler cards
Missing, expired and expiring cards, and locations without a certified manager.
Allergen matrix against recipes
Allergens in a dish that the matrix does not declare, and free-from claims a recipe breaks.
Prime cost
Weekly food, beverage and labor against sales for each location.
Location comparison
Every location against the group median, on the same measures.
closing: Each one does one job, on your computer, from a file you export. Nothing is paid, refunded, sent or changed in your POS until a named person on your team says so. Pairs with G6daddy's restaurant-and-bar AI agent: that one talks with your guests, these check the back office.
